what: the Mooble, a small fey creature of the deep mines from an old tale, painted seriously, alone and wary. It is small, round and fluffy, with long, soft, thick cream-white fur covering every part of it, so thick that no skin shows anywhere: its chest, belly, arms and legs are all hidden in fluffy fur, with no bare skin and no folds. Its head is big and round and sits straight on its round body with no neck. It has a flat, round, furry face with two small round black eyes set wide apart and a tiny round dark nose, no snout and no muzzle; two small rounded furry ears; short stubby furry legs with small dark paws; short furry arms with small dark hands. It has no tail. From its shoulders grow two small wings, each only as big as one of its hands: little leathery bat wings of dark charcoal-brown skin on thin dark finger bones. From the top of its head springs one dark antenna as thick as a finger: it rises a little, then bends forward and curls down in one loop, and the bobble hangs from its tip in the air just in front of its brow, between its ears, not touching its head. The bobble is a round bead as wide as one of its ears, dull dark red, unlit, giving no light at all; it has no stem and no leaf.
colours: long, soft, thick cream-white fur all over, two dark charcoal-brown leathery bat wings, dark eyes, a dark nose, dark paws and hands, a dark antenna as thick as a finger, a dull dark red unlit bobble.
holds: It holds nothing; both small hands are empty, raised in front of its chest.
pose: Seen from the front and a little from the side: it crouches low on its two short legs, knees bent, body hunched and drawn in, both small empty hands raised in front of its chest, peering warily at the viewer from the corner of its eyes, ready to bolt. Its two wings are folded shut, lying closed against its back like a furled umbrella. Exactly two arms and two legs.
action: It is frozen in a wary crouch, tense and still, like a small wild animal that has just been seen and is deciding whether to run.
